fields.meta_description: Build a ladder inspection form crews fill out on a phone, with failed ladders marked Do not use and every check saved to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Ladder Inspection Form Your Crews Fill Out on Site
fields.hero_description: Build a ladder inspection form that logs each check by ladder ID and takes any ladder that fails out of service.
fields.features_subheading: Describe your ladders and who inspects them. Emergent builds the form and a register that tracks the status of every ladder.
fields.feature_1:
Every ladder picked by its ID

Give every ladder a number once, such as L-07 or EX-12, and the worker picks it from a list on the form. Each check is saved against that ladder with a name and a time.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that match the ladder type

Each check is a short pass or fail list. A step ladder asks about its spreaders and locks, while an extension ladder asks about the rope and pulley that raise its upper section.
fields.feature_3:
One failed item, ladder out of service

A failed check changes the ladder's status to Do not use in the register. The safety manager gets an email naming the ladder and the item that failed, with a link to the record.
fields.feature_4:
A photo whenever an item fails

Add a photo field that opens only when an answer is Fail. The worker photographs the crack or the bent rung from the form, and the picture stays attached to that ladder's history.
fields.feature_5:
Inspections signed by the inspector

The inspector signs the monthly inspection on a phone or tablet once the last ladder is checked. The signature and date are saved with every pass or fail answer from that round.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to your own servers

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and host it anywhere. Teams that run their own safety system can fold the ladder records into it there.

fields.tab_content_1:
With all 8 checks passed, L-07 is in use by 7 AM

Tollworth Hardware checks each step ladder before its first climb of the shift. At 6:52 AM, stocker Stavros Ikonomou picks L-07 on his phone and answers 8 pass or fail questions on the feet, steps, spreaders, and locks. All 8 pass, the check is saved under L-07, and the ladder is in use when the store opens at 7 AM.
fields.tab_content_2:
After one cracked rail, EX-12 is out of service

Rafael Gallardo sets up 28-foot extension ladder EX-12 on a Hartsgrove Roofing job and checks it before he climbs. He marks the left side rail Fail for a crack near the base and adds a photo. The form sets EX-12 to Do not use and emails safety manager Tereza Folau the ladder, the failed item, and a link to the photo.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each month, 14 van ladders and one signature

Once a month, Yolanda Hennessy inspects the 14 ladders that ride on Velloran Electric's service vans, van by van in the yard. Of the 14, 13 pass, and ladder V-09 goes for repair with a bent rung lock. When the last ladder is done, she signs the inspection on her tablet, and it is filed with all 14 results.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which of 32 ladders are out of service or overdue

Ottercreek Property Management owns 32 ladders across 4 buildings, and the register shows each one with its status and next monthly inspection. Two are marked Do not use. Three inspections are overdue, the oldest at Harbor Court by 9 days. A repaired ladder stays at Do not use until it passes a new inspection.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Ladder Inspection Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a ladder inspection form that logs every check by ladder and acts on failures, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the checks for each type
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put a check before each shift
fields.howto_step_1_des: Walk each site and list every ladder by type and location, whether it stands free or is fixed to a wall. Give each one a short ID such as L-07 and label it on a rail. Every check on the form then names one ladder from this list.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Split the questions by ladder type. A step ladder needs its spreaders and locks looked at, and an extension ladder its rope and rung locks. Keep each item a plain pass or fail, and use the manufacturer's label on the ladder as a starting point.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a short pre-use check for the first climb of every shift, separate from the longer scheduled inspection. Keep it to what a worker can see and test by hand, and short enough to finish at the foot of the ladder in a minute or two.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for a photo on any Fail answer, mark the ladder Do not use in the app, and name who gets the email, such as the safety manager. The status in the app sits alongside the physical tag a crew hangs on the ladder itself.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Build a second, longer form for scheduled inspections. The inspector works through every ladder at one site, sends failures for repair, and signs at the end. Choose the interval that fits your sites, such as monthly, and the register shows the next due date.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give each ladder a register row with its status and its next inspection date. A ladder back from the repair shop should clear a fresh inspection before anyone changes its status. Sort the overdue inspections to the top of the list.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test on one site, then roll out
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the form to Emergent and run it on one site for a week. Fail a spare ladder on purpose to see the email arrive and the status change. Adjust anything by prompt, then share the link with every crew.

faq_plan.q: What is a ladder inspection form?
faq_plan.a: A ladder inspection form is the record of one check on one ladder. It names the ladder by ID and location, lists each part with a pass or fail answer, and records who checked it and when. A Fail answer also notes what is wrong.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a ladder inspection form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the form to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: your ladder types, the checks for each, and who hears about a failure. Emergent builds a checklist per ladder type, a register of every ladder, and the database behind both. Change anything later by prompting. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should an extension ladder inspection form cover that a step ladder one does not?
faq_plan.a: An extension ladder adds parts a step ladder lacks: the rope and pulley, the rung locks that hold the fly section, and the guide brackets between the sections. Look for a frayed rope and locks that do not seat fully. A step ladder brings its own items instead, such as the spreaders.

faq_plan.q: Can a school custodial staff use a ladder inspection form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Number the ladders by building, such as GYM-02 for the gym's 12-foot ladder, and custodians check each one before they climb it. Emergent builds the rest of a school's paperwork the same way from a prompt, including parent conference forms for teachers.

faq_plan.q: How often should a ladder inspection form be filled out?
faq_plan.a: In general industry, OSHA's rule says ladders are inspected before initial use in each work shift, more frequently as necessary, to identify visible defects. For construction, OSHA's ladder rule says ladders shall be inspected by a competent person for visible defects on a periodic basis and after any occurrence that could affect their safe use.

faq_plan.q: What should a ladder inspection form record when a ladder fails?
faq_plan.a: The failed item, a photo of the defect, who found it, and the ladder's change to Do not use. OSHA's general industry rule says a ladder with structural or other defects is immediately tagged Dangerous: Do Not Use or with similar language, and removed from service until repaired or replaced. The form is the record; the tag goes on the ladder itself.

faq_plan.q: How do I track ladder repairs on a ladder inspection form?
faq_plan.a: Add a repair note to each ladder's record that says what was fixed and who fixed it. Parts can be ordered through a supply request form linked from the same record. Keep the original Fail answer and its photo in the ladder's history, next to the repair.

faq_plan.q: Can workers fill out a ladder inspection form on their phones?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The form opens from a link in a phone browser, and a worker attaches a photo straight from the camera. Emergent sets no response caps on forms. A crew that checks 40 ladders a day never runs into a monthly limit.

faq_plan.q: How can a ladder inspection form show which ladders are overdue?
faq_plan.a: Give each ladder a due date for its next periodic inspection, and the register lists every ladder past it. Filter that list by site or ladder type before a walkthrough. The records sit in a database you own, and the history stays with the company when the safety manager changes.

faq_plan.q: Should a ladder inspection form use pass or fail answers or a rating scale?
faq_plan.a: Use pass or fail. A ladder either goes into use or it does not, and a 3 out of 5 on a side rail leaves the worker to decide which. Rating scales fit judgments with a range, such as a tryout evaluation form.

plan.angle: The results for this query are printable ladder checklists (PDF, Word, Etsy downloads) and university or state OSHA checklists that list what to look at. None shows what happens after a box is ticked: which ladder was checked, who checked it, what happens to a ladder that fails, and how a safety manager sees which ladders are due. This page shows a working ladder inspection form for four moments (the pre-shift check, a failed ladder, the periodic inspection by a competent person, the ladder register), with every inspection saved to a database the company owns. OSHA wording is quoted from the two ladder standards; no safety guarantees and no compliance claims.
